Librogame.title: Mycroft's Fortieth-Birthday Watch
Librogame.author: Luca Santarelli

Changes.Change: Rewritten for this engine: the twenty-nine paragraphs, and where each one leads, are those of the original
The sheet's opening, which already has its own two exits, is scene 1; paragraph 1 of the original, the servants' hub, is scene 30
The nine boxes at the foot of the sheet are a visible counter, and every accusation adds one
Each suspect can be accused only once: there are nine boxes and nine suspects
The cross-references in brackets are no longer read out: the buttons do that work

Librogame.ContentWarnings: None. A drawing-room mystery, with no blood and no violence.
Librogame.Blurb:
You have just reached for the violin when Lestrade knocks at the door: a gold watch, a personal gift from the Queen, has vanished from Mycroft's study at the Diogenes Club. Three people were in the room when it happened, and your brother is furious.
Question them, examine the scene, get the servants talking. Then point the finger. Every accusation ticks a box: compare your result with your friends' — who did best?

Page.Text: You are reaching for the violin when Inspector Lestrade knocks at the door. "Holmes, a theft at the Diogenes! A precious gold watch has vanished from Mycroft's study. Three people were present at the time of the theft: Lord Cavendish, Doctor Wilson and Miss Adler. Can we count on your help?" Do you take the case, or refuse?
You may question Lord Cavendish, Doctor Wilson, Miss Adler, or make another choice.

At the Diogenes. Mycroft is furious: "A theft in my own study! Besides being a personal gift from the Queen, if it is applied as a seal it carries the force of a royal order! I suspect one of the three guests is the culprit. Find the watch and the thief!" The game is afoot!
"Miss Adler, are you in such a hurry to leave London?" She laughs. "How do you know, Holmes? Yes, I have a performance in Paris!" But in her bag you catch a suspicious glint.
"Holmes raised one finger in the great silence: he spoke a name... and high above rang out a whinny!" Watson will write one day in his memoirs.
You find traces of ash on Mycroft's desk: you cannot recall ever seeing him smoke! You also notice a note on the desk: it is handwritten in a very dark blue ink.
Doctor Wilson puts down his pipe as the footman carries away the full ashtray. "I was in the library, absorbed in my studies. Cavendish is in financial difficulty. If I were you I should look there!"
The inspector is incredulous; he cannot tell whether you are serious. Your brother steps in.
Mycroft is curt. "I have left everything exactly as I found it!"
"I shall pretend I did not hear that..." Mycroft is giving you another chance: think again about all the clues!

Choice.text: Think again about all the clues

Page.Text: Lestrade puts a finger to his mouth after touching Wilson's sleeve. He looks at you, puzzled: "It tastes of blueberry..." You have got it wrong, Sherlock!

"The clues all point in the same direction..." you say, letting the silence build "...a false trail!" Lestrade, following your instructions, seizes the footman so that you can pull off his mask: it is Moriarty! Mycroft allows you a rare smile. "Well done, Sherlock."
Lestrade grills the cook for hours, and the only thing he gets out of him is his grandmother's cake recipe. "Holmes, that deduction of yours... it smells of burning!"

Irene Adler smiles, absently handing an empty glass to the footman. "What am I doing here? Ask your brother! My dear Holmes, I would never steal a man's watch. I did think, however, that I saw Wilson going towards the study. If we have finished..."
"Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth!" Your moment has come: at whom do you point the finger?

Lord Cavendish, a nobleman come down in the world, twists his moustache as the footman hands him a cup of tea. "I was reading the newspaper, Holmes. I never left the sofa! I did hear the Adler woman arguing with Mycroft shortly before the theft, though."

Choice.text: Press him, suspecting he is lying

Page.Text: The footman answers you deferentially. "I saw Doctor Wilson walking up and down outside Mr Mycroft's study, unable to make up his mind."
Irene takes two lace gloves from her bag and puts them on, laughing. "My dear Holmes, I had no idea you were fond of silk as well!" You have got it wrong, Sherlock!

You look more closely at Wilson: there is a small, very dark stain on his cuff. "Doctor, you say you were studying, but you have no books with you. What are you hiding?" Wilson stammers: "I-I only wanted to see the watch! But then it was gone..."
According to the cook, after the theft the footman reported having accidentally bumped into Miss Adler. Something fell out of her dropped bag, and she snatched it up in great haste.
You notice marks of forcing on the lock, but one detail strikes you: a minute scrap of blue cloth caught between the doors of the cabinet. Cavendish is wearing a blue overcoat!
"The footman told me himself: for some time now Cavendish has been asking a lot of questions about picklocks and suchlike tools! From riches to rags! And if I say so..." the stable hand reveals.
You may question the suspects, examine the scene of the crime, or talk to the servants. When you have finished, make an accusation.

Choice.text: Examine the scene of the crime

Page.Text: Under pressure, Cavendish gives way: "All right! I am drowning in debt, I wanted to sell the watch! But somebody took it before I could!"
Lestrade turns Cavendish inside out like a sock, overcoat included, and the overcoat proves to be perfectly whole. You have got it wrong, Sherlock!
You find a black glove on the floor. It is lace, of the kind Irene wears. You try it on: it fits you perfectly.
"The gentleman here pres—" you are about to finish the sentence when you see Mycroft's glare growing steadily grimmer, and you decide to be serious.
... courgettes, potatoes, sweetcorn, two hundred grams of ham, green tea...
"I am playing the violin," you answer, bored. Lestrade shakes his head in disappointment. The case is never solved and the watch vanishes for ever.
Ask about Lord Cavendish, Irene Adler or Doctor Wilson.
